ai.literal: Those who desire their wife glorious benefit will not attain; those who desire action an undesired thing indeed is that.
ai.translation: Those who are infatuated with their wives will not attain great achievements; such infatuation is also an undesired thing for those who desire to accomplish great deeds.
ai.modern: மனைவியை மட்டுமே விரும்பி அவளது வழி நடப்பவர்கள் சிறந்த நன்மைகளை அடைய மாட்டார்கள்; செயல்களைச் செய்து முடிக்க விரும்புகிறவர்களுக்கும் அது வேண்டத்தகாத ஒரு செயலாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against being overly infatuated with one's wife to the neglect of one's duties. The poet states that those who are consumed by domestic infatuation ('மனைவிழைவார்') will fail to achieve great and glorious results ('மாண்பயன் எய்தார்') in life. Furthermore, for those who are dedicated to accomplishing great deeds ('வினைவிழையார்'), such submissiveness is an undesirable trait ('வேண்டாப் பொருள்'). The verse emphasizes that greatness requires focus on duty rather than being ruled by domestic desires.

ai.literal: Without considering (his duty), the wealth of him who desires a woman will bring shame as a great shame.
ai.translation: The prosperity of a man who, disregarding his own duty, is infatuated with his wife, will only bring him a great and humiliating shame.
ai.modern: தன் கடமையை மதிக்காமல், தன் மனைவியின் விருப்பத்தையே விரும்பி நடப்பவனுடைய செல்வமும் பெருமையும், அவனுக்குப் பெரிய அவமானத்தையே தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against losing one's self-respect and sense of duty by being overly submissive to one's wife. The word 'pēṇātu' means not cherishing or neglecting one's duties and self-respect. When a man is infatuated ('viḻaivāṉ') with a woman to the point of neglecting his responsibilities, any wealth or status ('ākkam') he possesses will not bring him honor. Instead, it will only result in a great, public disgrace ('nāṇāka nāṇu tarum') that makes him a laughingstock.

ai.literal: The lack of natural character of being submissive towards one's wife, at all times, among noble people, shame will bring.
ai.translation: The unmanly nature of bowing submissively to one's wife will always bring shame when one stands among worthy men.
ai.modern: தன் மனைவியிடம் பணிந்துபோகும் ஆண்மையற்ற குணம், எப்போதும் நல்லவர்களிடையே அவமானத்தையே தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the loss of social dignity that comes from being overly submissive to one's wife. The phrase 'இல்லாள்கண் தாழ்ந்த' refers to behaving subserviently to the mistress of the house, and 'இயல்பின்மை' (literally, 'lack of natural character') denotes a lack of the strength and independence expected of a householder. Such submissiveness, the poet warns, will 'எஞ்ஞான்றும்' (always) bring 'நாணு' (shame or embarrassment) when the man stands 'நல்லாருள்' (among noble or worthy people). It emphasizes that a man who loses his authority at home cannot command respect in the wider society.

ai.literal: He who fears his wife, who does not possess the next life, his action-capability attaining greatness is not.
ai.translation: He who fears his wife and has no hope of the next life will never attain greatness in the strength of his actions.
ai.modern: மனைவிக்கு அஞ்சுகின்ற, மறுமைப் பயன் இல்லாதவனுடைய, செயல் செய்யும் ஆற்றலின் சிறப்பானது ஒருபோதும் விளங்குவதில்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the consequences of a man being subservient to his wife. The poet states that a man who lives in fear of his wife is like someone who has no share in the virtues of the next life. Such a person's capability and strength in executing actions will never achieve greatness or distinction. The key words 'வினையாண்மை' (strength of action) and 'வீறு' (greatness) emphasize that fear of one's wife paralyzes a man's capacity for noble and effective deeds.

ai.literal: He who fears his wife will indeed fear, at all times, doing good deeds to good people.
ai.translation: He who stands in fear of his wife will always shrink from performing noble deeds for virtuous people.
ai.modern: தன் மனைவிக்கு அஞ்சி வாழ்பவன், நல்லவர்களுக்கு நல்ல உதவிகளைச் செய்வதற்கு எப்போதும் பயப்படுவான்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains how domestic submissiveness destroys a man's social and moral agency. A man who is dominated by and fears his wife (இல்லாளை அஞ்சுவான்) loses his independence to act righteously. Consequently, he will always hesitate and fear (அஞ்சும்) to perform charitable or noble deeds (நல்ல செயல்) for worthy, good people (நல்லார்க்கு). The particle 'மற்று' emphasizes the certainty of this moral paralysis.

ai.literal: Even if they live than the celestials, those who fear the bamboo-resembling shoulders of their wife indeed have no dignity.
ai.translation: Even if they live with the splendor of the immortal gods, those who live in fear of their wife's bamboo-like shoulders possess no true dignity.
ai.modern: மனைவியின் மூங்கில் போன்ற தோள்களுக்கு அஞ்சி வாழ்பவர்கள், தேவர்களைப் போல வாழ்ந்தாலும் பெருமை இல்லாதவர்களே ஆவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the loss of honor for men who are overly submissive to their wives. The poet uses the classical metaphor of 'bamboo-like shoulders' (அமையார்தோள்) to describe the wife, representing her beauty and feminine grace. A husband who fears his wife instead of leading with mutual respect loses his dignity (பாடு). Even if such men enjoy a life of supreme comfort and longevity like the immortal gods (இமையார்), they are deemed completely devoid of greatness.

ai.literal: Than the manliness of conducting oneself doing a woman's command, a modesty possessing woman indeed possesses greatness.
ai.translation: A modest woman possesses far greater dignity than the manliness of a man who lives carrying out the commands of his wife.
ai.modern: மனைவியின் ஏவல்களைச் செய்து வாழ்கின்ற ஆணின் ஆண்மையைக் காட்டிலும், நாணமுடைய பெண்ணே பெருமை உடையவள் ஆவாள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares the submissive behavior of a man who obeys his wife's commands with the natural modesty of a woman. The author states that a woman who possesses a natural sense of shame or modesty (நாண்) is far more dignified and great than a man who loses his independence by acting according to a woman's dictates. The contrast is drawn between 'ஆண்மை' (manliness) which is compromised by subservience, and 'நாண்' (modesty) which elevates a woman's stature. Thus, true greatness lies in maintaining one's natural role and self-respect rather than yielding to improper dominance.

ai.literal: Friends' need they will not fulfill; good deeds they will not perform; she of the beautiful forehead's desire accordingly those who conduct themselves.
ai.translation: Those who live only to please the desires of their beautiful-browed wives will neither relieve the needs of their friends nor perform any virtuous deeds.
ai.modern: அழகிய நெற்றியை உடைய மனைவியின் விருப்பப்படி நடப்பவர்கள், தம் நண்பர்களின் தேவைகளை நிறைவேற்ற மாட்டார்கள்; அறச் செயல்களையும் செய்ய மாட்டார்கள்.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against losing one's independence by becoming entirely subservient to a spouse's whims. The phrase 'நன்னுதலாள்' refers to a wife with a beautiful forehead, and 'பெட்டாங்கு ஒழுகுபவர்' describes a husband who acts solely to satisfy her desires. Such submissiveness isolates a person from their wider social duties. Consequently, they fail to help their friends in times of need ('நட்டார் குறைமுடியார்') and neglect their moral obligation to perform virtuous deeds ('நன்றாற்றார்') for society.

ai.literal: Virtuous deeds and, abundant wealth and, other deeds and, woman's command with those who carry out, do not exist.
ai.translation: Virtuous deeds, abundant wealth, and other worthy pursuits of life will not be found with those who blindly carry out the commands of their wives.
ai.modern: மனைவியின் ஏவலுக்குப் பணிந்து நடப்பவர்களிடம் அறச்செயல்களும், சிறந்த செல்வமும், இன்பம் தரும் பிற நற்செயல்களும் இருக்காது.
ai.explanation: This couplet warns against being entirely subservient to one's wife's commands. It states that a man who merely obeys his wife's biddings loses three key aspects of a fulfilled life: 'aṟaviṉai' (virtuous deeds), 'āṉṟa poruḷ' (abundant wealth), and 'piṟaviṉai' (other meaningful actions or pleasures). The word 'ēval' means command or bidding, highlighting that blind obedience destroys a man's independent capacity to perform his duties and earn respect.

ai.literal: To those who possess a spacious mind joined with wisdom, at all times, the folly arising from being attached to a woman does not exist.
ai.translation: For those who possess a spacious mind filled with wisdom and deliberation, the folly of being subservient to a wife never occurs.
ai.modern: ஆராய்ந்து அறியும் அறிவு பொருந்திய பரந்த மன வலிமை உடையவர்களுக்கு, மனைவியின் வழிப்பட்டு நடப்பதால் உண்டாகும் அறியாமை எப்போதும் உண்டாகாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the antidote to being ruled by domestic attachment. It states that individuals who possess a spacious mind filled with wisdom and systematic deliberation are immune to this weakness. Their intellectual depth and strength of character prevent them from blindly yielding their judgment to their wives. Thus, true wisdom and mental strength naturally protect a person from the folly of submissiveness.
